I'm partway through tracing where the comment gets printed twice. The evidence so far is enough to name the likely functions, so I'll stop here. I haven't run Prettier to confirm the fix.

- **Comment printing is split across two places.** `willPrintOwnComments` returns true for a `superClass` of any class. That tells the generic comment printer to skip it, so the class printer is responsible.
- **JSX also prints its own comments.** `printJsxElement` wraps its output in `printComments`. `isJsxElement` is also a blanket true in `willPrintOwnComments`.
- **The class printer skips JSX superclasses.** In `printClass`, the `extends` branch only calls `printComments` for non-JSX superclasses. It assumes the JSX printer already handled the comments.
- **The comment ends up outside the parentheses.** The output shows a copy before the parentheses, and in the second example after them. Parentheses come from `needsParentheses` through `parent-needs-parentheses.js`. I haven't checked how that code interacts with the comments, so that is the part I'm least sure of.

The `printClass` extends branch and `printJsxElement` are the two functions that decide who prints the comment, so they are the first places to change. `willPrintOwnComments` is the other candidate.

The comment is printed twice because two printers each claim it for a JSX superclass. I read the code but didn't run the reproduction, so I haven't confirmed which path produces the outer copy.

- **`willPrintOwnComments` (`will-print-own-comments.js:28`):** it returns true for `key === "superClass"` on a class. It also returns true for any JSX element. The generic printer therefore skips comments on the superclass.
- **`printJsxElement` (`jsx.js:768`):** it calls `printComments` itself, which gives the inner `(/* c */ <div />)`.
- **`printHeritageClauses` / `printSuperClass` in `class.js`:** the code at `class.js:118-128` also calls `printComments`, unless the node is JSX without an ignore comment. The outer `/* c */` therefore comes from this class-level path.

The fix is to make exactly one of these own the superclass comments. The leading comment must end up inside the parentheses and the trailing comment must stay inside them as well.

`class.js:118` is the code that decides whether the class-level path prints the comments. `will-print-own-comments.js:28` and `printJsxElement` decide who owns them.

The `handle-comments.js` function that covers class comments (`handle-comments.js:327`) is a weaker lead.

The bug is in how Prettier prints link URLs in Markdown. I read the code but didn't run the playground input.

`[test](/hello?foo&quot\;bar)` is parsed by remark, and the link's `node.url` comes out as `/hello?foo"bar`. The `\;` was an escape, so the parser dropped the backslash. `printUrl` then calls `escapeCharacterReferences`, which only escapes `&` when `characterReferenceRegex` matches. `"` is a character reference, so the result should be `&quot\;`. But the output shows `"` with no backslash, so the regex doesn't match here. The decoded URL looks like a character reference, so on the second pass it gets decoded to `"`. I didn't open `characterReferenceRegex`. Its definition is just above line 456 in the same file.

The fix is probably in `printUrl` or `escapeCharacterReferences`. Either the regex has to match this case, or the escaping has to be done differently. `printTitle` also calls `escapeCharacterReferences`, so a change there affects titles too.

The `link` case in `genericPrint` (the function containing the `case "link"` at line 168) is the caller. It probably doesn't need to change.

I didn't check the exact start lines of `genericPrint` or `printTitle`, so those are guesses and I've left them out of the list.

The report's input shows all three attributes quoted, but the expected output keeps `unquoted={data}` unquoted. So I read the bug as: with `--embedded-language-formatting off`, an unquoted LWC `{data}` value gets quotes added. I only read the code and did not run it, so I haven't reproduced this.

The decision about whether to keep a value unquoted is made in `shouldUnquoteAttributeValue`. It has two callers:
- `printAttributeValue` in `src/language-html/print/attribute.js` is the printer used when embedded formatting is off. It calls `shouldUnquoteAttributeValue` and otherwise always wraps the value in quotes.
- `printAttribute` in `src/language-html/embed/attribute.js` is the embed path and makes the same check.

`isAttributeValueQuoted`, which `shouldUnquoteAttributeValue` calls, is the other likely culprit. It decides whether the source value was quoted by comparing the value span's length to `value.length + 2`. If that comparison is wrong for LWC attributes, the unquote path is skipped and quotes get added.

I'd start with `shouldUnquoteAttributeValue` and `isAttributeValueQuoted`, then check `printAttributeValue`.
